item.title: India to have one of the 'best' trade deals with the US: Piyush Goyal
item.description: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday said India will have one of the "best" trade deals with the US in every respect. He said that India has negotiated a very good set of outcomes with the US in the pact. "And in every respect, India will have one of the best deals with the US," he told reporters here. India and the US in February finalised a framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the tariff landscape in the US have led to further negotiations.

item.title: Nearly 70% of PLI scheme segments on track, says NITI Aayog report
item.description: A sector-wise assessment of PLI scheme shows that nearly 70 per cent of the targeted segments are on track, with particularly strong outcomes emerging in electronics, telecom and pharmaceuticals drugs, NITI Aayog said in a report on Thursday. As of March 2026, cumulatively the scheme has attracted investments of Rs 2,40,138 crore, generated production worth Rs 22,66,412 crore, created employment for 8,49,069 individuals, and disbursed Rs 35,354 crore in incentives. "The assessment indicates that the production linked incentive (PLI) scheme is beginning to generate meaningful additionality across several sectors. "...the sector-wise assessment of PLI scheme indicates that nearly 70 per cent of the targeted segments are broadly on track, with particularly strong outcomes emerging in electronics, telecom and pharmaceuticals drugs," the report 'Impact Assessment of PLI Schemes' said. The report pointed out that large scale electronics manufacturing (LSEM) with an outlay of Rs 34,193 cr

item.title: Moody's raises India's FY27 growth forecast to 7% on broad-based momentum
item.description: Moody's Ratings on Wednesday said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience. In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to "intensifying and broadening price pressures", with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6 per cent target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand. "India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," it said. Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7 per cent over
item.bs:keywords: Moody's Ratings, India GDP growth, FY27 growth forecast, 7% growth, Indian economy, private investment, capital expenditure, inflation, El Nino, southwest monsoon, RBI monetary policy, energy supply shock
